explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/672: can the product of an AP n, n+d, …, n+(k−1)d of positive integers with k ≥ 4 and (n,d) = 1 be a perfect power? Erdős believed not. Erdos672With k l says that for every k-element s ⊆ ℕ that is an AP with first term n > 0, difference d > 0 and gcd(n,d) = 1, the product is not an l-th power. Following the @[question] convention, the statement is the proposition asked: ∃ k ≥ 4, l > 1 with ¬Erdos672With k l. Faithful (the expected answer is no, so this is believed false).
